To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a numerical approach based on the use of an adaptive mesh to the SPHE technique and the cohesive zone law can be successfully adopted to model the fragmentation of the projectile and the tile, with the advantage of conserving the mass of the projectile and tile, and of avoiding discontinuities in the contact between the projectile and tile.

the fragmentation of a BSP impacting a ceramic tile is well reproduced using a 3D Lagrange finite element model, in which the projectile is modelled as a pre fragmented assembly of sub parts with the possibility of separation of the parts when the cohesive law is met, and the ceramic tile is modelled as an assembly of solid and SPH elements.

a new approach to the fragmentation of a projectile impacting a tile is proposed, based on the transformation of the SPH technique to the finite element method, and the cohesive law to the fragmentation of the projectile.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an innovative numerical tool for the simulation of the impact of BSP on ceramic tiles, which allows a more realistic representation of the fragmentation phenomena, with respect to classical approaches, in order to better predict the residual velocity and to analyse the wave propagation and the damage morphology of the ceramic tile.
the development of an original approach to the fragmentation of brittle materials by means of the SPH technique.
the numerical modelling of the fragmentation phenomenon of a BSP impacting a ceramic tile.

the proposed modelling approach is able to reproduce with a good degree of accuracy the fragmentation of both projectile and ceramic tile, with a significant saving of computational time.

the use of the cohesive law and the transformation of the elements in SPH particles is a promising way to model the fragmentation of brittle materials, with the advantage of avoiding the discontinuity of the contact surface between the parts.

it is possible to model fragmentation in an alternative way, with the possibility of using adaptive meshes, and that the results of the model are comparable with the results of the classical finite element analysis.
